questions.q: What are they to do when they would see a stray animal of a fellow Israelite?
questions.a: They are to return the animal to its owner. If the owner is not nearby or they do not know who he is, they should take the animal to their own house until the owner comes searching for it and then return it to him.

questions.q: What did Moses tell them to do when they see an animal of a fellow Israelite fallen down in the road?
questions.a: They must help their fellow Israelite lift it up again.

questions.q: What is an abomination to Yahweh?
questions.a: It is an abomination to Yahweh for a woman to wear men’s clothing or a man to wear women’s clothing.

questions.q: What should the people of Israel do if they find a mother in a bird’s nest with her young or sitting on the eggs?
questions.a: They must let the mother go, but the young they may take for themselves.

questions.q: What is required when an Israelite builds a house?
questions.a: It is required that he put a railing around the roof so he would not be guilty of causing someone’s death if anyone fell from it.

questions.q: What would happen if the Israelites plant their vineyards with two kinds of seeds?
questions.a: If they plant their vineyards with two kinds of seeds, all the produce of the seed and the yield of the vineyard would have to be set apart.

questions.q: What were the Israelites instructed to make for the four corners of their garments?
questions.a: They were instructed to make tassels for the four corners of the garments with which they covered themselves.

questions.q: What must happen if a man has made a false accusation against his wife saying she was not a virgin?
questions.a: The elders of the city must punish the man. They must fine him 100 silvers and give it to the girl’s father. Also, she shall remain his wife, and he can never send her away.

questions.q: What should happen if the proof of the wife’s virginity is not found?
questions.a: If they cannot find proof of her virginity, then she must be brought out and stoned to death because she has done a disgraceful thing.

questions.q: What must happen if a man is found lying with a woman married to another man?
questions.a: Both the man and the woman must be put to death to make sure no one else from Israel does this evil action.

questions.q: Why are the people of Israel instructed to stone to death both a girl who is engaged to a man and another man if they are found lying together?
questions.a: They are instructed to stone both of them because the girl did not cry out and the man defiled the one who is engaged to be the wife of a fellow Israelite.

questions.q: What must happen if the man forces the engaged girl to lie with him when they are out in a field?
questions.a: If this happens out in a field, then the man must die, but nothing must be done to the girl because he found her out in the open countryside and even though she cried out, there was no one there to rescue her.

questions.q: What must happen if a man lies with a girl who is a virgin, but who is not engaged and they are discovered?
questions.a: The man who lay with her must give 50 silvers to the girl’s father, and she shall become his wife and he may never divorce her.

questions.q: What must a man not take from his father as his own?
questions.a: A man must not take his father’s wife as his own.

commentary.text: Verses 1–4 If we duly regard the golden rule of “doing to others as we would they should do unto us,” many particular precepts might be omitted. We can have no property in any thing that we find. Religion teaches us to be neighbourly, and to be ready to do all good offices to all men. We know not how soon we may have occasion for help.

God's providence extends itself to the smallest affairs, and his precepts do so, that even in them we may be in the fear of the Lord, as we are under his eye and care. Yet the tendency of these laws, which seem little, is such, that being found among the things of God's law, they are to be accounted great things. If we would prove ourselves to be God's people, we must have respect to his will and to his glory, and not to the vain fashions of the world. Even in putting on our garments, as in eating or in drinking, all must be done with a serious regard to preserve our own and others' purity in heart and actions. Our eye should be single, our heart simple, and our behaviour all of a piece.

These and the like regulations might be needful then, and yet it is not necessary that we should curiously examine respecting them. The laws relate to the seventh commandment, laying a restraint upon fleshly lusts which war against the soul.
